title: Keel's Solana swaps are bookended by Borrow and Repay instructions that enforce atomicity and slippage in one transaction
content:
A.6.1.1.3.2.6.1.2.2.2.1.2.1.2.3 describes the AtomicSwap action as "split across two instructions which are applied as bookends to inner swap instructions." The Borrow action "temporarily funds the Relayers account with tokens to support an intended swap on a permitted swap route, subject to rate limits and validating that the corresponding `Repay` instruction is present at the end of the transaction" (…3.1). The Repay action "validates that the proceeds of the swap meet minimum slippage requirements, or fails the overall transaction" (…3.2).

The pattern solves a problem specific to routing through third-party venues. To swap on an external AMM, the relayer must temporarily hold the funds — but funds in a relayer's own account are outside the Controller's protection. The bookends narrow that window to a single transaction and make it self-enforcing: Borrow refuses to release funds unless the returning Repay is already in the instruction list, and Repay refuses to let the transaction settle unless the value that came back is within tolerance.

This is the flash-loan idiom repurposed as an internal safety mechanism rather than as a product. Custody is lent, not transferred, and the loan's terms are checked by the same program that granted it.

It also explains why maximum slippage is an admin-only setting on the Ethereum side. The slippage bound is the *only* thing standing between a permitted swap route and an arbitrary value transfer to a counterparty, so the party that sets it must not be the party that uses it.
description: Borrow temporarily funds the relayer for a swap on a permitted route only if a matching Repay is present at the end of the transaction;
